title: Came Alone, Can Barely See

patient.name: Mr Krishnan s/o Subramaniam
patient.presenting_complaint: Severely reduced vision in both eyes; came alone by public transport and is having trouble finding his way around the clinic

history.hpc: Mr Krishnan has advanced eye disease with severely reduced vision in both eyes. He came alone by bus and train. He says: 'I cannot see well already, I come by myself, just now I nearly trip at the door.' He is at clear risk of falling while navigating the clinic. The PSA must complete a fall-risk (PFAER) assessment and take active measures.
history.pmhx: Advanced glaucoma and diabetic eye disease, both eyes. Hypertension.
history.social_hx: Lives alone; limited family support. Travelled alone today.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Advanced disease; severely reduced vision both eyes
examination_findings.fundus: Known advanced pathology, for doctor review

investigations.fall_risk_assessment: Fall-risk (PFAER) assessment: high risk — severe bilateral visual impairment, elderly, unaccompanied, already had a near-trip on arrival, in an unfamiliar busy environment. Active guidance and supervision are required throughout the visit.

diagnosis: High fall risk on PFAER assessment driven by severe visual impairment in an unaccompanied elderly patient. The PSA competency is identifying the high risk and actively guiding/supervising the patient and arranging escort support, not merely documenting it.

immediate: Complete the PFAER fall-risk assessment and recognise the high risk from severe visual impairment
Personally guide the patient, offering an arm and describing the route and any obstacles
Seat him safely in a clear, well-lit area with an unobstructed path, away from clutter
Accompany him for each move (to testing, to the doctor, to the exit) rather than letting him navigate alone
Arrange staff/volunteer escort and inform the nurse he is high fall risk and unaccompanied
Document the fall-risk assessment and the actions taken
follow_up: Doctor to review his eye condition
Arrange escort to public transport/taxi at the end of the visit
Flag in records that he needs an escort and ideally a companion for future visits, and consider social support referral
patient_education: Reassure him that staff will guide him around safely
Encourage him to ask for help to move rather than walking alone
Discuss coming with a companion in future and accepting escort help
Advise on keeping to clear, well-lit paths to reduce trips and falls

key_points: Establishes the severe bilateral visual impairment
Identifies that he came alone and nearly tripped on arrival
Notes the unfamiliar, busy environment as an added risk
Completes the PFAER fall-risk assessment at this visit
Identifies severe visual impairment plus unaccompanied status as key risks
Recognises the high risk despite no other acute change
Classifies the patient as high fall risk
Recognises visual impairment as the dominant risk factor
Understands the unaccompanied status compounds the risk
Knows high risk requires active guidance, not just a note
Personally guides and supervises the patient and offers an arm
Seats him safely and keeps paths clear
Arranges escort and informs the nurse; documents the assessment
Advises on companions/escort and considers social support referral
